A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ParoQuant. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments measuring perplexity, reasoning and non-reasoning accuracy, throughput, training cost and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results, revises EfficientQAT reasoning scores and adds original weight-activation quantization results in Tables A2–A3.

M1.justification: New Section A.3 extends ParoQuant to W4A4 by quantizing transformed activations alongside weights. This adaptation replaces decoder-level optimization with sequential per-linear optimization using quantized upstream outputs, and replaces weight fine-tuning with GPTQ. The original W4A16 method remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The training corpora and perplexity, reasoning and commonsense task coverage are retained. Section A.3 explicitly reuses the existing evaluation setup; its new numerical formats and activation precision change experimental configurations, not datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds a distinct W4A4 comparison suite: SpinQuant and FlatQuant for INT4, and MR-GPTQ for MXFP4. FlatQuant was previously only cited, MR-GPTQ is newly introduced, and SpinQuant previously participated in weight-only perplexity comparisons. Existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Section A.3 adds INT4 and MXFP4 W4A4 evaluation settings, with GPTQ used for weight quantization across the compared methods. Previously documented W4A16 splits, context lengths, metrics and optimization budgets are unchanged; the revised EfficientQAT scores are not accompanied by a stated protocol revision.

E4.justification: The transform, optimization-stage, calibration-data and rotation-count ablations in Tables 5–6 and the effectiveness analyses in Figures 2 and A1 are retained. The new W4A4 tables benchmark the adapted method without adding controlled ablations, robustness tests or error analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed averaging for GPQA and AIME, one seed for MMLU-Pro, and the same 100-seed Hadamard sampling procedure. v2 introduces no new uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables A2–A3 add results for both W4A4 formats: INT4 reasoning accuracy is 63.6 for ParoQuant versus 61.7 for SpinQuant and 63.9 for FlatQuant; MXFP4 gives 61.4 versus MR-GPTQ's 62.5. Table 2 also revises EfficientQAT's scores and average from 55.4 to 55.6, reducing the stated ParoQuant advantage from 6.5 to 6.3 points. Existing ParoQuant scores and throughput results are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Equation (10) defines the W4A4 output as Q(XT^-1)Q(TW)+b, extending the formulation to quantize both transformed operands. The independent-pair and independent-rotation definitions and existing mathematical reasoning are retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the contribution from weight-only PTQ to include weight-activation quantization, newly claiming accuracy matching leading methods in that setting. The retained 2.4% reasoning improvement over AWQ and less-than-10% overhead claims are explicitly scoped to weight-only quantization.

C2.justification: Section A.3 newly reports decoder-level convergence failures and unstable weight fine-tuning under W4A4, explaining the procedural adaptations. It labels the extension preliminary and not specifically tuned for W4A4. Its favorable interpretation of MR-GPTQ comparisons overlooks the lower reasoning accuracy shown in Table A3.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a project website on the title page and documents GPTQ use across the W4A4 comparisons and reuse of the existing evaluation setup. The original hardware, software versions and detailed W4A16 hyperparameters are retained. The new tables do not explicitly identify their evaluated model.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the MR-GPTQ microscaling work and QSPEC, removes FPTQuant, and brings the previously cited quantized-reasoning study into the introduction. These are targeted positioning updates accompanying the W4A4 extension; the broader related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive localized revisions, a W4A4 appendix subsection is inserted, and subsequent appendix sections are renumbered. Author, affiliation, acknowledgment and publication-header text also change. Most exposition and the main section structure are retained.

P2.justification: Two W4A4 tables are added as Tables A2–A3. The existing throughput and training-cost tables become A4–A5 and move with the appendix reflow. Existing figures and main-table structures are retained, with limited spacing and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: The W4A4 adaptation, comparisons and explicit optimization limitations provide useful evidence about applicability beyond v1's weight-only scope while preserving the original evidence. The gain is limited by sparse identification of the new experimental setup and an overbroad superiority claim: Table A3 reports worse reasoning accuracy than MR-GPTQ, 61.4 versus 62.5, despite better perplexity and non-reasoning accuracy.
